restaurants.desc: Classic Shanghai home-style cooking with Bund views — great value. Locals return for the braised pork and glazed ribs.
tips: Go for dinner for Bund views
Say 靠窗的位置 for a window seat

restaurants.desc: Michelin Bib Gourmand. Hand-made dumplings by aunties. Go at 10am or 3pm to avoid peak queues.

dishes.en: Crab roe and pork xiaolongbao (8 pcs)

tips: Ask for ginger vinegar: 姜丝醋

restaurants.desc: Century-old snack shop on Nanjing Road. The egg yolk pork floss rice ball is legendary.

dishes.en: Egg yolk and pork floss rice ball

restaurants.desc: Shanghai street food legend. Crispy pork chop meets chewy rice cake, drenched in sweet-spicy sauce.
tips: Order both — they are a combo
The house spicy sauce is the secret

restaurants.desc: One of Shanghai oldest pan-fried bun shops. Crispy golden bottom, juicy pork filling. Pair with curry beef soup.
tips: Bite the side first — hot soup inside
Made in batches — short wait for fresh ones

restaurants.desc: Historic Shanghai bakery since 1928. The whipped cream chestnut cake is an icon.
tips: Worth visiting for the history alone

restaurants.desc: Old-school rice cake shop. Fresh-made rice cake rolls with youtiao, pickled veg and pork floss.
Iconic state-run food store. The butterfly cookies are the go-to Shanghai souvenir.
tips: Great for gifts to bring home

restaurants.desc: Premium crab banquet with Bund views. Crab roe noodles are outstanding. Request a window seat.
tips: Ask for window seat: 我要靠窗的位置

restaurants.desc: Locals top pick for Japanese BBQ. Exceptional value. The curry stone pot rice is unmissable.
Upscale hotpot with exceptional fish maw chicken broth. Great for a splurge.
tips: Order the broth — it is the star

restaurants.desc: Considered the best Japanese BBQ in Shanghai by many locals. Premium cuts, self-grill.
Old-school Shanghai institution. Hard to book — a sign locals actually eat here.
tips: Tianping Rd branch is the one

restaurants.desc: One of Shanghai most acclaimed restaurants. Exceptional Zhejiang cuisine — special occasion dining.
Lively HK-style open kitchen. Satisfying portions, great value, casual atmosphere.
Charming French wine bar on Changle Road. The braised frog pasta is what everyone talks about.
tips: Changle Road — great area for the evening

restaurants.desc: Honest Fujian-style seafood noodle soup. Zero tourist pretension. Deeply savoury broth.
Named after Lu Xun famous story. Authentic Shaoxing wine-culture cuisine with literary atmosphere.
tips: Literary decor, great for curious travellers

restaurants.desc: Creative Taiwanese restaurant. The stir-fried Want Want crackers sounds odd but tastes extraordinary.
tips: Popular with young locals and expats

restaurants.desc: Most authentic Malaysian restaurant in Shanghai. The Ipoh seafood river noodle is the signature.
Cosy izakaya. The tsukemen dipping noodles have incredible chew. Roasted pigeon leg is memorable.
tips: Order the tsukemen — that is the reason to come

restaurants.desc: Shanghai most reliable brunch spot. Consistently good food, friendly service, relaxed setting.
Michelin-starred roast duck. International visitors rave about it. Caviar duck skin is the signature.
tips: Book at least a week ahead
Bund branch for the best views

restaurants.desc: Beloved sauerkraut fish. The tangy pickled cabbage broth is addictive. Pair with fried rice.
tips: Order medium spice if new to Sichuan

restaurants.desc: Top-tier Fujian cuisine at the Bund. Acclaimed for exceptional seafood and refined flavours.
tips: Less famous than neighbours — easier to book
Ask staff for the day fresh catch

restaurants.desc: Neighbourhood institution for steamed pork buns and traditional pastries. Where grandparents shop.
tips: Great contrast to Nanjing Road shops

restaurants.desc: Excellent Peking Duck chain beloved by foreign visitors. Crispy skin dipped in white sugar changes people.
tips: Try skin with sugar first — sounds odd, tastes incredible

restaurants.desc: Favourite Spanish restaurant of the Shanghai expat community. The spicy potatoes alone are worth the visit.
Beloved Italian family restaurant. Expat families keep coming back for unpretentious home-cooking Italian.
tips: More casual than most Italian restaurants in the city

restaurants.desc: Mediterranean-vibe brunch cafe run by a foreign owner. Packed with expats on weekends.
tips: Go weekdays to avoid weekend crowds

restaurants.desc: Stylish modern Sichuan with dramatic teahouse interior. Top recommendation for impressing foreign guests.
tips: Perfect for first-time visitors to China

restaurants.desc: Atmospheric Yunnan restaurant near the Bund. Silk Road decor wows foreign guests every time.
tips: Interior design alone is worth visiting
Walk to the Bund afterwards — very close

restaurants.desc: Elaborate Chinese palace decor meets solid Cantonese cooking. Foreign guests love the theatricality.
tips: The decor is the draw — bring your camera

restaurants.desc: Creative Guizhou-Western fusion bistro on Anfu Road. Unique concept rarely seen outside China.
tips: Walk Anfu Road before or after
Higher price point — save for a special evening

restaurants.desc: Italian restaurant with top marks from expats and locals alike. Bilingual staff, handmade pasta.
Reliable all-day Western cafe popular with foreign residents. Good fallback when you need something familiar.
Elegant Italian dining in Xintiandi. Consistently recommended by the foreign community for special occasions.
Authentic Neapolitan pizza baked in a wood-fired oven. Italian expats say this is the real thing.
Proper British pub food in Tianzifang. Around 70% foreign crowd. Fish and chips done right.
tips: In Tianzifang — explore alleyways before eating

restaurants.desc: Michelin-starred Shanghai restaurant since 2021. Crab roe rice and braised pork are outstanding.
tips: Best value Michelin in the city

restaurants.desc: No-frills neighbourhood Shanghai restaurant open 30+ years. The scallion pork chop is legendary.
tips: Staff may not speak English — pointing works

restaurants.desc: Michelin favourite for 7 consecutive years. Unassuming exterior, exceptional cooking inside.
tips: Seven Michelin mentions — this is the real thing
Same street as Hai Jin Zi — visit both

restaurants.desc: Cult-favourite Chongqing hotpot. Six-time returnees call it the best in Shanghai.
tips: Choose 微辣 (mild) if new to hotpot spice
Book 3+ days ahead — fills up fast

restaurants.desc: Popular Chongqing hotpot near People Square. Fresh-cut beef is the signature.
tips: Order 微辣 (mild) or 中辣 (medium) if new to spice

restaurants.desc: Premium Chaoshan-style beef hotpot — not spicy at all. Ultra-fresh cuts in a clear broth. A must for beef lovers.
tips: NOT spicy — clear broth, pure beef flavour
Dip in house satay sauce: 沙茶酱

restaurants.zh: 滇牛云南酸菜牛肉火锅
restaurants.desc: Tangy Yunnan-style beef and sauerkraut hotpot. Lighter than Sichuan — great for spice-sensitive eaters.
tips: A gentler intro to Chinese hotpot
The sour broth is the point — lean into it

restaurants.desc: Popular Lebanese in Lujiazui. Great for vegetarians wanting a break from Chinese food.
tips: In Lujiazui — combine with evening Bund walk

restaurants.desc: Popular Yunnan chain that locals genuinely love. The black bean mashed pork is legendary.

dishes.en: Black bean mashed pork (hei san duo)

tips: Order 黑三剁 — locals number one reason to return

restaurants.desc: Creative Northwest China bistro that wowed locals when the owner of Xinrongji showed up to eat. Bold flavours — braised beef ribs in spicy sauce, garlic lamb, and a stunning bruschetta with braised cartilage and burrata.
tips: Go early — popular dishes sell out
Every dish is a surprise — trust the menu
Creative fusion of Northwest and Western techniques

restaurants.desc: Small, atmospheric creative bistro that locals keep returning to. Space is intimate, pasta has exceptional chew. Reservation essential — very hard to walk in.
tips: Reservation required — book at least a week ahead

restaurants.desc: The go-to for what locals call white people food (白人饭). The shakshuka (North African eggs) is famous. Consistently recommended by Shanghai locals as a reliable all-day bistro.
tips: Go on a weekday for a quieter experience
The shakshuka is the signature — order it
Casual, relaxed atmosphere — good for solo dining

restaurants.desc: Michelin 3-star chef Paul Pairet casual French bistro in Xintiandi. The real French toast is what everyone talks about — crispy outside, pillowy inside, paired with sour cream ice cream. Raw beef tartare is also excellent.

dishes.en: Beef patty with egg and mash

tips: Book ahead — popular at lunch and dinner
In Xintiandi — walk the area after eating
French toast is sweet — pair with the sour cream ice cream to balance

restaurants.desc: Beloved for its drunken chicken claypot and claypot rice — described by locals as a winter comfort food institution. Consistently recommended alongside the best Shanghai restaurants.
tips: The drunken chicken broth is the highlight

restaurants.desc: Hunan restaurant with a devoted local following — locals joke about being its unofficial shareholders. Bold, spicy, satisfying.
tips: Good for groups who enjoy spice
More authentic than most Hunan restaurants in the city

restaurants.desc: Top yakitori (grilled skewers) restaurant recommended by locals who avoid the Gubei area. Serious Japanese grilling technique, intimate atmosphere.
tips: Skip the Gubei branch — locals recommend other locations
Order the chef selection for best experience

restaurants.desc: Late-night buckwheat noodle shop with generous beef portions. A favourite for after-dinner second rounds. The cold buckwheat noodles with beef are the signature.

dishes.zh: 荞麦楞拌面配大份牛肉

tips: Order the large beef portion — worth it
Popular as a second stop after dinner elsewhere

restaurants.desc: The oldest and most established Spanish restaurant in Shanghai — open 20+ years at Sinan Mansion. The Valencia paella is the must-order. Celebrity-spotted, consistently top-ranked for Spanish cuisine in the city.
tips: Book ahead — two-floor restaurant with courtyard
The paella is the reason to come

restaurants.desc: Endorsed by Spanish expats as the most authentic tapas in Shanghai. The garlic shrimp alone signals the quality. No paella — pure tapas focus. Better than Tres Perros according to many Spanish visitors.
tips: Endorsed by Spanish expats — the real thing
The olives are considered the best in Shanghai by some

restaurants.desc: Spanish restaurant with a rooftop terrace — great for evening dining with a breeze. Iberian ham and seafood rice are the must-orders. One of the top 3 Spanish restaurants in Shanghai.
tips: One of the most consistent Spanish restaurants in the city

restaurants.desc: Shanghai French dining institution — been here for years and still considered the best classic French in the city. Black truffle pasta, beef eye fillet and foie gras are the signatures. Knowledgeable sommelier.
tips: The French institution of Shanghai — multiple years at the top
Enthusiastic sommelier — ask for wine pairing

restaurants.address: Far Eastern Hotel, People Square (人民广场前远东饭店)
restaurants.desc: Modern French restaurant at People Square that has dramatically improved with each new seasonal menu. Now considered must-visit level by serious Shanghai diners. The fried chicken with lemongrass sauce and the 20kg tomato reduction dish are highlights.
tips: Third seasonal menu is the one to try
Located in People Square — easy to get to

restaurants.desc: One of the most famous Western restaurants at the Bund. Creative French cuisine with Asian influences. Foie gras with sour cherry, king crab with sweet peas, Patagonian toothfish — all consistently excellent. Go for lunch for better light and photos.
tips: Go for lunch — better light for photos
Evening has more atmosphere but dishes come slowly
Worth every yuan for a special occasion
